questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.question:
Consider the following about the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC):
1. It was set up in 1964 on Santhanam Committee recommendations and gained statutory status under CVC Act, 2003
2. It comprises one Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners
3. It is appointed by the President on recommendation of a committee comprising PM, Home Minister, and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha
4. It has jurisdiction over all state government employees
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — CVC does NOT have jurisdiction over state government employees. Its jurisdiction covers: All India Services (Central deputation), Group A officers, senior officials in PSBs, RBI, NABARD, PSUs and insurance companies. State-level vigilance is handled by State Vigilance Commissions/Lokayuktas. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh January 2026.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.question:
With reference to the WEF Global Risks Report 2026 and India:
1. Cybersecurity was identified as the biggest risk for India in 2026
2. Income and wealth inequality is India's second biggest risk
3. Geoeconomic confrontation emerged as the top global risk overall
4. Climate-related risks dominate India's immediate risk profile
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — India's immediate risk profile shows stronger focus on SOCIETAL and GOVERNANCE-related risks (cybersecurity, inequality, insufficient public services) rather than climate. Climate risks dominate the GLOBAL long-term outlook (10 years), not India's immediate 2026 profile. India recorded 369.01 million malware detections in 2025. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh January 2026.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.question:
Consider the following about passive euthanasia in India:
1. The Supreme Court affirmed 'right to die with dignity' under Article 21 in Common Cause vs Union of India (2018)
2. Active euthanasia is illegal and classified as culpable homicide/murder under BNS, 2023
3. Living wills are legally recognized for advance medical directives
4. Physician-assisted suicide is legal in India with medical board approval
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — Physician-assisted suicide is NOT legal in India. Only PASSIVE euthanasia (withdrawal of life-support) is permitted under strict SC guidelines with two-stage medical boards. Active euthanasia and assisted suicide remain criminal offences under BNS 2023 (Sec 100 - Culpable Homicide, Sec 101 - Murder, Sec 108 - Abetment of Suicide). SC heard Harish Rana case (2025) for passive euthanasia. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh January 2026.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
With reference to India-EU Free Trade Agreement negotiations:
1. India and EU have been negotiating an FTA since 2007
2. India currently has no bilateral CEPA/FTA with any individual EU member state
3. Key sticking points include data localization, labour standards, and agricultural market access
4. EU is India's largest trading partner
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — EU is NOT India's largest trading partner. The US is India's largest trading partner followed by China. EU as a bloc is India's 2nd/3rd largest trading partner. India-EU FTA talks started 2007, suspended 2013, relaunched 2022. Key issues: EU demands on data adequacy, sustainability clauses, government procurement; India's concerns on agricultural subsidies, carbon border tax (CBAM). Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh January 2026.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's M.A.N.A.V. Vision for AI unveiled at India-AI Impact Summit 2026:
1. M stands for Moral & Ethical Systems
2. A stands for Accountable Governance
3. N stands for National Sovereignty
4. It views AI as autonomous force independent of human oversight
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — M.A.N.A.V. vision SHIFTS AI from autonomous force to becoming an EXTENSION of human aspirations. It is a human-centric framework. Full form: M-Moral & Ethical, A-Accountable Governance, N-National Sovereignty, A-Accessible & Inclusive, V-Valid & Legitimate Systems. India-AI Impact Summit 2026 recorded 2,50,946+ pledges for AI responsibility (Guinness World Record). Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh February 2026.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.question:
With reference to India's drone ecosystem as of 2026:
1. Over 38,500 drones are registered on the Digital Sky platform
2. PLI Scheme with ₹120 crore outlay supports domestic drone manufacturing
3. GST on drones was reduced to 5% to boost adoption
4. Namo Drone Didi scheme provides drones to Women SHGs for farming
questions.explanation: All correct. India's drone ecosystem has expanded rapidly under Drone Rules 2021 (amended 2022, 2023). Digital Sky platform: single-window for registration, certification. 38,500+ drones registered, ~39,900 Remote Pilot Certificates issued by Feb 2026. PLI scheme: ₹120 crore for drone & component manufacturing. GST reduced to 5%. Namo Drone Didi (Nov 2023): drones to Women SHGs for precision agriculture, pesticide spraying. SVAMITVA: 3.28 lakh villages drone-mapped. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh February 2026.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.question:
Consider the following about the Rajya Sabha:
1. It has a maximum strength of 250 members including 12 nominated by the President
2. Members are elected by proportional representation through Single Transferable Vote by elected MLAs
3. NOTA is applicable in Rajya Sabha elections
4. The domicile requirement for Rajya Sabha candidates was removed in 2003
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 4 correct. Statement 3 WRONG — Supreme Court in Shailesh Manubhai Parmar v. Union of India (2018) SCRAPPED NOTA for Rajya Sabha elections, holding that NOTA defeats the principles of proportional representation and STV. RS uses 'Open Ballot' system where party MLAs must show marked ballot to party agent. Domicile removed by RPA (Amendment) Act, 2003 — candidate can be elector from any parliamentary constituency. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh February 2026.

questions.subject: Social Issues
questions.question:
With reference to the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006 and tribal rights:
1. It recognizes both Individual Forest Rights (IFRs) and Community Forest Rights (CFRs)
2. Gram Sabhas have the authority to verify and approve claims under FRA
3. The Act addresses historical injustice from the colonial Indian Forest Act, 1878
4. Over 90% of all FRA claims filed have been approved across India
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — 45%+ claims have been REJECTED in some regions. Overall approval rates vary significantly by state. Issues: resistance from Forest Department, misuse of technology (VanMitra platform) in low-connectivity areas, Gram Sabhas sidelined in many states. Colonial Indian Forest Act 1878 based on 'eminent domain' treated communities as trespassers. FRA 2006 aims to rectify this by recognizing pre-existing rights. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh February 2026.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.question:
Consider the following about Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY):
1. It provides health cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalization
2. Pre-existing diseases are covered from Day 1
3. Funding pattern is 60:40 (Centre:State) for normal states
4. All citizens of India are eligible under the scheme
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — NOT all citizens are eligible. AB-PMJAY targets the bottom 40% (~12 crore families/55 crore people) based on SECC 2011 deprivation criteria. However, in Sept 2024, all citizens 70+ years were covered under Ayushman Vay Vandana Card (~6 crore elderly). 42 crore+ Ayushman cards issued; ~11 crore hospital admissions by Dec 2025. NITI Aayog study found 65% patients still paid out-of-pocket in private hospitals. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh March 2026.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
With reference to India's IndiaAI Mission:
1. It has an outlay of over ₹10,300 crore
2. It covers AI compute infrastructure, data, skilling and innovation
3. IndiaAI Compute Portal provides shared access to GPUs/TPUs
4. India's AI governance follows a blanket regulatory approach like the EU AI Act
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — India does NOT follow a blanket regulatory approach like EU AI Act. India's approach is 'pro-innovation' with SECTORAL guidelines (RBI for banking AI, SEBI for algo trading, IRDAI for insurance AI) rather than comprehensive legislation. AI Governance Guidelines 2025 emphasize trust, equity, accountability. IndiaAI Mission includes: IndiaAI Kosh, AI Data Labs Network, MeghRaj GI Cloud. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh February 2026.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question:
Consider the following about Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) and India:
1. CBDC is a digital form of a country's fiat currency issued by the central bank
2. RBI has proposed linking BRICS countries' CBDCs at the 2026 BRICS Summit hosted by India
3. India's digital rupee pilot was launched by RBI in 2022
4. CBDCs eliminate the need for any banking infrastructure
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — CBDCs do NOT eliminate need for banking infrastructure. They still require digital infrastructure, wallets, settlement systems, and potentially work through commercial banks as intermediaries. RBI proposed BRICS CBDC interlinking for the 2026 summit, building on 2025 BRICS Rio Declaration on payment system interoperability. India's e-Rupee pilot: wholesale (Nov 2022) and retail (Dec 2022) segments. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh January 2026.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question:
With reference to India's Economic Survey 2025-26:
1. It advocates 'strategic sobriety' over defensive pessimism for managing global volatility
2. It proposes 'strategic indispensability' rather than mere resilience
3. It is prepared by the Chief Economic Adviser
4. Its recommendations are binding on the government
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — Economic Survey recommendations are NOT binding on the government. It is an analytical/advisory document presented to Parliament one day before the Union Budget. It provides assessment of economy and suggests policy direction but government is not obligated to follow. Survey 2025-26 emphasized capability building towards Viksit Bharat @2047. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh February 2026.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
Consider the following about sodium-ion batteries:
1. They use sodium instead of lithium as charge carrier
2. Sodium is far more abundant and cheaper than lithium
3. They are suitable for grid-scale energy storage
4. They have higher energy density than lithium-ion batteries
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — Sodium-ion batteries have LOWER energy density than lithium-ion (typically 100-160 Wh/kg vs 150-250 Wh/kg for Li-ion). Their advantages are: abundance (sodium is 1000x more plentiful than lithium), lower cost, better low-temperature performance, non-flammable electrolytes. Best suited for: grid storage, stationary storage, short-range EVs — not high-performance applications. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh February 2026.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question:
With reference to Carbon Capture, Usage and Storage (CCUS):
1. CCU converts captured CO2 into useful products like chemicals, fuels, and building materials
2. CCS involves storing CO2 in underground geological formations permanently
3. India has dedicated geological storage sites for CO2 already operational
4. CCUS is considered essential for decarbonizing hard-to-abate industries like steel and cement
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 4 correct. Statement 3 WRONG — India does NOT yet have dedicated operational geological CO2 storage sites. India is in early stages of CCUS development. NITI Aayog has released reports on CCUS potential. Key applications: steel, cement, refineries (hard-to-decarbonize). CCU products: synthetic fuels, chemicals, polymers, building materials (carbon-cured concrete). CCS: deep saline aquifers, depleted oil/gas reservoirs. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh February & March 2026.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question:
Consider the following about India expanding its Ramsar Network:
1. India expanded its Ramsar Network to 98 sites as of 2026
2. Ramsar sites are wetlands of international importance designated under the Ramsar Convention, 1971
3. India has the highest number of Ramsar sites in South Asia
4. Designation as Ramsar site prohibits all human activities in the wetland
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — Ramsar designation does NOT prohibit all human activities. The convention promotes 'wise use' of wetlands — sustainable utilization compatible with conservation. Activities like fishing, agriculture (in buffer zones), ecotourism may continue. The convention emphasizes balancing human needs with ecological integrity. India: 98 sites (2026), largest in South Asia. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh February 2026.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
With reference to LIGO-India Gravitational Wave Observatory:
1. It is India's first gravitational wave observatory
2. It is being set up in Maharashtra
3. It is a collaboration between India and the US (LIGO Laboratory)
4. Gravitational waves were first directly detected in 2015 confirming Einstein's prediction
questions.explanation: All correct. LIGO-India is being built at Aundha in Hingoli district, Maharashtra. It is a collaboration between LIGO Lab (Caltech/MIT), IndIGO consortium (Indian Initiative in Gravitational-wave Observations), and DAE/DST. First gravitational waves detected by LIGO in Sept 2015 (merger of two black holes 1.3 billion light-years away) — confirmed Einstein's 1915 General Relativity prediction. 2017 Nobel Prize awarded to Rainer Weiss, Barry Barish, Kip Thorne. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh March 2026.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's counter-terrorism strategy PRAHAAR:
1. It is India's National Counter-Terrorism Policy and Strategy
2. It integrates intelligence fusion through a Multi-Agency Centre
3. It addresses hybrid threats combining terrorism, cyber attacks and disinformation
4. It was formulated exclusively for dealing with Left Wing Extremism
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — PRAHAAR is NOT exclusively for LWE. It is a comprehensive national counter-terrorism strategy addressing ALL forms: cross-border terrorism, urban terrorism, lone-wolf attacks, hybrid threats, cyber warfare, and disinformation. It advocates whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach. Key elements: real-time intelligence fusion via MAC, stronger cyber/financial surveillance under PMLA 2002, integrated security via National Security Strategy. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh March 2026.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.question:
With reference to the death penalty in India:
1. Supreme Court has not confirmed any death sentences in the past three years (as of 2025)
2. The 'rarest of rare' doctrine governs its application in India
3. Juveniles, pregnant women, and mentally ill persons cannot be executed
4. The President's pardoning power under Article 72 is not subject to judicial review
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — President's pardoning power under Article 72 IS subject to judicial review. SC can review on grounds of: non-application of mind, arbitrariness, extraneous considerations. SC confirmed zero death penalties in last 3 years; 10 acquittals in 2025. Death row: 574 prisoners (Dec 2025, highest since 2016). BNS 2023 retains death penalty for ~14 offence categories. Manoj v. State of MP (2022) mandated mitigation reports. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh February 2026.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP):
1. It covers vaccination against 12 vaccine-preventable diseases
2. India achieved 98.4% full immunisation coverage by January 2026
3. India produces approximately 60% of global vaccine supply by volume
4. Mission Indradhanush targets areas with zero immunisation coverage only
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — Mission Indradhanush (2014) targets both UNVACCINATED and PARTIALLY vaccinated children and pregnant women, not just zero-coverage areas. It focuses on hard-to-reach, urban slums, and low-coverage areas. Intensified Mission Indradhanush (2017) further expanded. Coverage rose from 62% (2015) to 98.4% (Jan 2026). India: 3rd globally in pharma (volume), exports to ~200 countries, supplied 298M COVID doses to ~100 countries. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh March 2026.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question:
With reference to Hybrid Electric Vehicles (HEVs) vs Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs):
1. HEVs use both internal combustion engine and electric motor
2. HEVs do not require external charging infrastructure
3. BEVs produce zero tailpipe emissions while HEVs still have some emissions
4. FAME scheme equally subsidizes both HEVs and BEVs
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — FAME (Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Electric Vehicles) primarily subsidizes BEVs and plug-in hybrids, NOT conventional HEVs equally. HEVs self-charge through regenerative braking and ICE, hence need no external charging. They are a transition technology. BEVs: zero tailpipe emissions, fully electric. India's EV push prioritizes BEVs for long-term decarbonization. Source: Drishti IAS Saraansh March 2026.
